newsitem.title: USA: Municipal elections could slow Bosnia pullout.
newsitem.headline: Municipal elections could slow Bosnia pullout.

text.p: Municipal elections expected in Bosnia this year could slow the rate of withdrawal of peacekeeping troops there, but that removal will be completed within "several weeks" after December 20, NATO's top military officer said on Wednesday.

U.S. Army General George Joulwan, the allied commander of all NATO forces in Europe, refused to predict whether a follow-on international military force would be sent to Bosnia next year after the 58,000 NATO-led peacekeepers are removed.

"This is a very delicate time. We are getting into some bad weather ... with municipal elections coming up," Joulwan told reporters at a Pentagon news conference. He said he would insist that a "capable force" remain in Bosnia to help provide security for those elections at some 4,500 polling stations.

"If there are going to be municipal elections before the end of our (December 20 withdrawal) mandate, my recommendation would be that that drawdown would be limited" until the elections and then speeded up after then, he said.
"I think we will have several weeks (after December 20) before we get the force out," he said of the NATO-led peace implementation force (IFOR), which includes more than 15,000 U.S. troops.

"Let's not pre-judge ... let us see what happens in the municipal elections," added Joulwan, refusing to support predictions from top western officials that a follow-on force to IFOR would be needed to keep peace in Bosnia next year.
